stories.title: AlphaProof Code
stories.reason: DeepMind is open-sourcing formal-verification artifacts from an agentic multi-LLM system that machine-checked Signal's cryptographic protocol — verifiable, security-relevant, and backed by a real primary source.
key_facts: Agentic multi-LLM framework formally verified Signal's compiled cryptographic protocol code
Generated 6M+ lines of Lean proof code over 4 weeks; flagged ~1% of the codebase for human review
When 2 previously-fixed bugs were reintroduced into an isolated copy, the system produced machine-checked proofs the buggy versions were insecure
DeepMind says it is open-sourcing the formal-verification artifacts (not model weights)

stories.title: Fireworks AI Confirms Wider Breach Affecting Customer Datasets, Model Weights and Notion AI Chats
stories.reason: AI supply-chain compromise: attacker breached Fireworks' R&D environment and exfiltrated incomplete model weights/datasets plus Notion AI chat transcripts — hits the always-surface model-supply-chain-compromise topic directly.
key_facts: Attacker first used stolen credentials on 2026-10-06; reached Fireworks' R&D dev environment via a third-party cloud provider on 2026-10-23
Exposed data includes incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers, plus billing info and API keys
Notion disabled its Insights feature and stopped serving open-weight models through Fireworks; said <1% of workspaces affected
Attackers linked to a group that resells stolen LLM access ('LLMjacking')

stories.title: CWE-bench v2: More coverage, quality, and transparency
stories.reason: New cyber-eval benchmark release with real multi-model numbers, gated dataset, and open grader/harness — strong fit for the eval-methodology and security-benchmark always-surface topics.
key_facts: 100 public tasks across 91 CWEs; agent must find+fix a real security weakness in a repo without breaking tests
Gemini 4 Argon: 67.8% pass@1 / 81.0% pass@4; Claude Opus 5.5: 67.3% / 78.0%
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash hits 57.0% pass@1 at $0.04/rollout vs Opus 5.5's $1.83 and Argon's $3.92
Dataset gated on Hugging Face (collinear-ai/cwe-bench); runs via Harbor; held-out set protects leaderboard integrity

stories.title: SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
stories.reason: Real-world RCE in an open-source inference engine (SGLang) breached live AI agents inside a TEE — concrete agent-infra attack, though no CVE or public PoC yet.
key_facts: RCE in SGLang let an attacker run code on a NEAR AI inference server running inside a TEE
18 AI agents on an older non-TEE deployment were accessed; ~100 Private Chat users had account data downloaded
Two customer NEAR AI Cloud API keys were exposed in logs and revoked
No CVE number or public PoC disclosed; fix deployed to all inference servers

stories.title: Compress any LLM 3x in one click,near-lossless,in under 50 MB RAM
stories.reason: 4-bit quantization framework with real code/kernels and a public repo — fits the quantization always-surface topic — but the vendor's 'near-lossless 3x/50MB' framing overstates the measured 2.8-3.31x VRAM compression and the writeup has internal inconsistencies.
key_facts: Asymmetric Group-32 microscaling, no calibration data, outlier channels kept FP16 (up to 3%); custom Triton kernels
Measured compression 2.80x-3.31x VRAM (not a flat 3x); e.g. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B 3.31GB → 1.03GB, 82.53 tok/s with CUDA Graph
WikiText-2 perplexity rose 33.83 → 34.73 (+0.90) vs FP16
Code at github.com/NeuraCryption/SPECTRA; some table/figure inconsistencies and a mismatched model link found on inspection

stories.title: How Well Does AI Peer Review Work? A Benchmark Built from 100 Planted Errors
stories.reason: Concrete, reproducible eval of AI review tools against 100 planted errors in real papers — good benchmark-criticism fit, though false-positive rate wasn't measured and no direct repo link was found on the page.
key_facts: 100 known errors planted across 10 open-access psychology papers, run through frontier models + 2 commercial AI review tools
Best single system caught 71/100 errors; worst caught 30/100; pooled across all systems caught 93/100
7 errors missed by every system, all omissions (deleted info) rather than inserted mistakes
False-positive rate not measured; paper claims public data/logs but no direct repo link found on the page

stories.title: An Open Field Guide to Inference Engineering
stories.reason: Solid curated reference on inference-serving internals (KV-cache sizing, batching/quantization/speculative decoding, engine choice) — matches the 'how models are served' priority, but it's vendor-authored synthesis, not original research.
key_facts: Llama 3 70B needs ~320KB KV cache/token at FP16, so a 128K-token context needs ~40GB
Orca reports 36.9x throughput over static batching; vLLM cut KV-cache waste from 60-80% to <4%
A 320B MoE model needs ~320GB at FP8; one real checkpoint came in at 177.7GB vs a 315GB dtype estimate
Written by Modelplane/Upbound, vendors in this space — numbers not independently verified

stories.title: From Attack Surface to Defense Architecture: Compositional Security for Agentic Coding Harnesses
stories.reason: Concrete, quantified defense against agentic-coding-harness attacks (LLM-judge vs deterministic guards) with real numbers — good AI x cyber fit, but it's a self-reported arxiv paper with no public repo or demo found.
key_facts: 252 test fixtures (120 attack, 120 benign, 12 multi-step kill chains)
LLM-judge guard: 98.3% refusal of benign work at 142.3ms latency vs deterministic Ring-0 guards: ABR 1.000/FPR 0.000 at 12.7µs (~11,200x faster)
Stateless baseline missed 4/12 multi-step attack chains; coarse boolean taint blocked 83.3% of benign workflows
No code repository, demo, or released system found on the paper's page
